title: One Point at Monte Rei
title_candidates: The Steadiest Man Wins by One
theme: A tournament of wild extremes — 17 eagles, two all-time scoring records, and a 10 at a par 3 — decided by a single point on the final green, where Alex Baker's banked opening round outlasted Gregg Williams's four-round pursuit.
opening_hook: Open on the 17th green in R4: Alex Baker takes 8 at the hardest hole but one (SI 3) and hands Gregg Williams the outright Trophy lead with one hole left (b01, b17) — then rewind to the 43 points Alex Baker banked at Quinta da Ria in R1 that made such a finish survivable at all.

trophy_storyline.subject: How Alex Baker turned a 43-point opening round at Quinta da Ria into a one-point win, surviving a 10 and an 8 in R4
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: It is the closest kind of TEG win there is — one point, settled on the last green — and the man who won it was outscored in three of the four rounds by the man who lost it.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: Alex Baker opens with 43 points at Quinta da Ria, eagling the par-5 11th and the par-5 16th (b33, b26) and leading by 10; over R2–R4 he posts 38, 39 and 37, never finishing a round better than third of five, while Gregg Williams closes a gap that was once 11 points down to one (b42, b30). Turn: on the R4 back nine Alex Baker bleeds 8 shots from the 9th to the 11th (b44), retakes the outright lead at the 12th (b29), then drops 11 shots in three holes including a 10 at the par-3 14th (b02, b24) and an 8 at the par-4 17th, SI 3, which hands Gregg Williams the lead with one hole to play (b01, b17). Resolution: a birdie at the par-5 16th had already stopped the bleeding (b13), and a par at the 18th put Alex Baker back in front (b19) for a 157-point win by one (b06) — his third Trophy, built on the one round he won and the steadiness that followed, and taken because Gregg Williams ran out of holes. Earlier form to fold in: the sextuple-bogey 11 at Monte Rei's 18th in R2 (b20) and the quadruple-bogey 8s at the 3rd in R3 and R4 (b45, b16).
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Wins It at the Last
Alex Baker Loses It, Then Takes It Back
trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Wins It at the Last
trophy_storyline.standfirst: Leader since the 9th hole of R1, the defending champion handed the TEG 19 Trophy to Gregg Williams with an 8 at the 17th and needed only a par at the 18th to take it straight back.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams goes +27, +14, +13, +12 to win the Green Jacket by fourteen after starting the tournament bottom of the field
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: It is a 14-stroke gross win and Gregg Williams's own best gross aggregate, taken off a player with nine prior Jacket wins, and it came from the man propping up the field after R1.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: Jon Baker led the TEG 19 Green Jacket after R1 and R2 by two, while Gregg Williams opened +27 and sat last in the field on the Trophy metric. Turn: at Monte Rei's par-3 7th in R2 Jon Baker took 8 and Gregg Williams 6, ending a 20-hole lead (b40); the two traded the lead through that back nine before Gregg Williams took it outright at the 2nd in R3 and never gave it back, eagling the par-5 16th in R2 and the par-5 8th in R3 and R4 (b15, b10, b03). Resolution: best gross round of the field in both R2 and R4, a record-equalling two-hole run of birdies at the 5th and 6th in R4 (sr01, b50, b35), 13 birdies or better across the tournament — an all-time TEG record (sc03) — and a +66 that beat David Mullin by 14 (b08).
headline_candidates: Williams Cuts Fifteen Shots in Three Rounds
Williams Takes the Jacket by Fourteen
From Bottom of the Field to Green Jacket
jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: Williams Cuts Fifteen Shots in Three Rounds
jacket_storyline.standfirst: Gregg Williams went +27, +14, +13, +12 at Monte Rei to claim the TEG 19 Green Jacket, beating nine-time holder David Mullin by fourteen strokes for his own best gross total.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker eagles twice, posts the best round of R2, leads the Jacket — and still retains the Wooden Spoon by seven
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Spoon holder kept it back-to-back despite producing the single best round of the field in R2, which makes the other three rounds all the more conspicuous.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: Jon Baker arrived as reigning Wooden Spoon holder from TEG 18, opened with 33 points at Quinta da Ria including an eagle at the par-5 11th (b72), and led the Green Jacket from the 5th hole of R1. Turn: in R2 he was the best man in the field with 44 points — eagles at the par-5 2nd and the par-5 16th (b68, b58) and 19 points across the closing five holes (b36) — having already lost the gross lead at the 7th that morning (b40). Resolution: 33 and 33 followed, last in the field in both R3 and R4, and the TEG 19 Wooden Spoon retained on 143 points, seven adrift of David Mullin (b57).
headline_candidates: Jon Baker Eagles Twice, Finishes Last
Forty-Four Points, and Still the Spoon
Jon Baker Keeps the Spoon by Seven
spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: Jon Baker Eagles Twice, Finishes Last
spoon_storyline.standfirst: Two eagles and the best round of R2 were not enough to stop the reigning holder keeping the Wooden Spoon, seven points adrift of David Mullin.

discovered_storylines.subject: Seventeen eagles, all of them on par 5s, plus two all-time scoring records and a record-equalling birdie streak of two holes
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Seventeen eagles across the field is the defining statistical fact of TEG 19, and every single one arrived on a par 5 — the 2nd, 8th, 11th and 16th did most of the scoring in this tournament.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 at Quinta da Ria sets the pattern immediately — John Patterson eagles the par-5 11th and the par-5 16th (b25, b21), with Alex Baker (b33, b26), Gregg Williams (b27), David Mullin (b32) and Jon Baker (b72) all cashing in on the same two holes. Turn: Monte Rei's par 5s prove no harder, with the 2nd, 8th and 16th yielding eagles in R2 (b22, b18, b15, b68, b58), a double eagle-fest at the 8th and 16th in R3 (b10, b11, b04, b05) and Gregg Williams again at the 8th in R4 (b03) — 17 in all (b79). Resolution: the record book takes the hit, with Gregg Williams's 13 birdies or better an all-time TEG record (sc03) and the sternest gravitas reserved for two separate two-hole birdie streaks — Gregg Williams at the 5th and 6th, John Patterson at the 16th and 17th — each tying the all-time TEG record of, in total, two (sr01, sr02).
headline_candidates: Seventeen Eagles, Every One a Par Five
The Par Fives Paid Out All Tournament
Record Broken: Two Birdies in a Row
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Seventeen Eagles, Every One a Par Five
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The 2nd, 8th, 11th and 16th gave up eagle after eagle across four rounds, and two of the field equalled an all-time TEG streak record that stands at precisely two holes.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin sets all-time TEG records for eagles and birdies in one tournament and finishes fourth of five
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Nobody in TEG history has scored like David Mullin did here — five eagles and 13 birdies or better — and it bought him second from bottom on the Trophy and a 14-stroke defeat in the Jacket he has won nine times.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: David Mullin's R1 at Quinta da Ria contains an eagle at the par-5 11th (b32) and a septuple-bogey 11 at the 15th that drops him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race (b49, b152). Turn: the eagles keep coming — the 2nd and 8th in R2 (b22, b18), the 8th and 16th in R3 (b11, b05) — five in all, an all-time TEG record, alongside 13 birdies or better, also an all-time record (sc01, sc02). Resolution: the arithmetic refuses to cooperate, with a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 15th and a 7 at the 9th in R4 (b43, b48) leaving him fourth of five on the Trophy and 14 gross strokes behind Gregg Williams in the Green Jacket.
headline_candidates: Mullin Rewrites the Record Book, Wins Nothing
discovered_storylines.standfirst: David Mullin set two all-time TEG scoring records in the Algarve and still finished second from bottom, an 11 at Quinta da Ria's 15th setting the tone for the shots in between.

discovered_storylines.subject: Monte Rei's par-3 7th, stroke index 8, quietly ruins four players across three consecutive rounds
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A mid-ranked short hole cost the field more than any of Monte Rei's supposed monsters, and it took the Green Jacket lead off Jon Baker into the bargain.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: in R2 the 7th takes 8 from Alex Baker (b47) and 8 from Jon Baker, whose 20-hole Green Jacket lead ends there as Gregg Williams escapes with a 6 (b40). Turn: R3 offers no learning whatsoever, with Alex Baker and Gregg Williams both walking off with quadruple-bogey 7s at the same hole (b38, b39). Resolution: Alex Baker returns in R4 for a quintuple-bogey 8 (b09) — three visits, three disasters, on a par 3 rated only the eighth hardest on the card.
headline_candidates: Three Rounds, Three Eights at the Seventh
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Stroke index 8 and 3 par at Monte Rei, the 7th extracted 8s and 7s from four different players in three consecutive rounds and settled the Green Jacket lead along the way.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The R4 birdies at the 16th steadied both Alex Baker and Gregg Williams, but neither is redemption — it was survival; tournament_shape.close_finish is true on a final margin of 1 with a decisive R4 lead change, so the counterfactual frame leads, with dual_narrative for the two men who carried the finish.

why_the_champion_won: Alex Baker banked 43 points at Quinta da Ria in R1 — 11 clear of Gregg Williams and the only round he won — then never finished a round worse than fourth of five as the steadiest man in the field, which was just enough: Gregg Williams outscored him in three of the four rounds, led by one at the 17th in R4, and ran out of holes.
